output.headline: Ratifies the minutes of the Board's Special Meeting of March 4, 2020
output.summary: The Board approves the written minutes of its Special Meeting on March 4, 2020, which staff prepared shortly after the meeting. This is routine record keeping with no cost.

output.headline: Awards Rook Electric $125,000 to maintain video surveillance systems at 30 sites
output.summary: Rook Electric was the lowest responsive bidder, so the district hires it to maintain video surveillance systems, including servers, software and cameras, at 30 sites. The Board also rejects all other bids. Work is scheduled from September 24, 2020 to July 9, 2021.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $25,920 for a consultant to support classroom drug education and health lessons
output.summary: A consultant will provide 648 hours supporting teachers, in online and in-person classrooms, on lessons about drug education, holistic health, and how race, law and politics affect incarceration and exploitation of youth, including a program called TUPE. The agreement is up to $25,920 from September 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021, and the Board is approving it after it began.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $45,000 for an arts consultant to help build the district's Strategic Arts Blueprint
output.summary: A consultant will work with the Visual and Performing Arts (VAPA) team to plan and carry out support structures that help district schools use the arts to improve learning. The agreement is up to $45,000 from August 3, 2020 to June 30, 2021. The Board is approving it after it began.

output.headline: Ratifies $14,037 for MCT Technology's Carecloud software for the Early Childhood program
output.summary: MCT Technology, Inc. provides Carecloud software for the Early Childhood program. It handles enrollment, eligibility, emergency contacts, electronic and contactless attendance, meal counts, licensing compliance and billing. The agreement is up to $14,037 from August 17, 2020 to June 30, 2021, and the Board is approving it after it began.

output.headline: Adds $215,050 to Ninyo & Moore's environmental testing contract for the Fremont construction project
output.summary: This amendment adds $215,050, including a $19,550 contingency, for more soil sampling and a technical memo requested by the Department of Toxic Substances Control at the Fremont New Construction Project. It raises the contract limit from $396,517 to $611,567 and extends it to August 17, 2021.

output.headline: Adds $28,189 to Ninyo & Moore's engineering contract for LaEscuelita Educational Center
output.summary: This amendment adds $28,189 for extra operations and maintenance consulting at the LaEscuelita Educational Center project, raising the contract limit from $48,340 to $76,529. It covers tasks that have already been completed plus more planned for 2020. It also extends the contract end date to June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Adds $11,857.10 for Nor-Cal Moving Services at the Glenview construction project
output.summary: This changes an existing moving contract with Nor-Cal Moving Services of Hayward. The added money pays to relocate two rooms and items from the gym into classrooms for the Glenview New Construction Project. The contract limit rises from $27,000.00 to $38,857.10, and all other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Hires Tulum Innovative Engineering for $98,000 phone and data cabling at Santa Fe
output.summary: The district chose Tulum Innovative Engineering of Oakland, through competitive bidding, to install about 300 data cables with patch panels and jacks for the Santa Fe special education site. The work covers about 85 phone lines, 143 computer lines and 4 fax lines. It is scheduled to run from September 24 to December 23, 2020.

output.headline: Adds $6,000 for Nor-Cal Moving Services on the Cole Administration move
output.summary: This changes an existing moving contract with Nor-Cal Moving Services of Hayward. The added money pays to move all furniture from the classrooms into the multipurpose room for the Cole Administration Move Relocation Project. The contract limit rises from $27,800.00 to $33,800.00, and all other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Pays Project Support Services $42,000 for state architect close-out help on school projects
output.summary: Project Support Services will help the district finish and certify construction projects with the Division of the State Architect (DSA), the state office that reviews school construction. The contract is up to $42,000 for work from September 24, 2020 to June 30, 2021. The item title says it was not competitively bid.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $95,200 a year for Bertrand Fox law firm to give the district legal advice through 2022
output.summary: Bertrand, Fox, Elliott, Osman & Wenzel will provide legal services and general legal advice to the district as needed, under a memorandum of understanding (MOU) and engagement policy. This is a paid legal engagement of up to $95,200 per fiscal year. It runs from July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2022, and the Board is approving it after it began.

vendor.name: Bertrand, Fox, Elliott, Osman & Wenzel Law Firm

The agreement is up to $46,080 from September 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021, and the Board is approving it after it began.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $25,000 for a clinical supervisor of mental health interns at ten elementary schools
output.summary: A clinical supervisor will provide 334 hours supervising graduate students in the Mental Health Intern Program, which places two interns at each of ten elementary schools. The agreement is up to $25,000 from August 10, 2020 to June 30, 2021. The Board is approving it after it began.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $90,000 for We Lead Ours to support classroom drug education and health lessons
output.summary: We Lead Ours will provide 2,250 hours supporting teachers, in online and in-person classrooms, on lessons about drug education, holistic health, and how race, law and politics affect incarceration and exploitation of youth, including a program called TUPE. The agreement is up to $90,000 from September 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021, and the Board is approving it after it began.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $25,000 for clinical supervision of the Newcomer Wellness Team's social workers
output.summary: A clinical supervisor will guide up to 8 unlicensed social workers and Marriage and Family Therapists on the district's Student Newcomer Wellness Team, in groups and one on one. The agreement is up to $25,000 from August 15, 2020 to May 28, 2021. The Board is approving it after it began.

output.headline: Approves 2020-21 special education services contract with 360 Degree Customer
output.summary: The district signs a master contract with 360 Degree Customer, Inc., a nonpublic school or agency, to provide services to students with special education needs during the 2020-21 school year. The terms follow Resolution No. 2021-0008. The item does not state a dollar amount.

output.headline: Approves 2020-21 special education services contract with North Valley School
output.summary: The district signs a master contract with North Valley School, a nonpublic school or agency, to provide services to students with special education needs during the 2020-21 school year. The terms follow Resolution No. 2021-0008. The item does not state a dollar amount.

output.headline: Approves 2020-21 special education services contract with Seneca Family of Agencies
output.summary: The district signs a master contract with Seneca Family of Agencies, a nonpublic school or agency, to provide services to students with special education needs during the 2020-21 school year. The terms follow Resolution No. 2021-0008. The item does not state a dollar amount.

output.summary: The district signs a master contract with Care Youth Corporation - Lava Heights Academy, a nonpublic school or agency, to provide services to students with special education needs during the 2020-21 school year. The terms follow Resolution No. 2021-0008. The item does not state a dollar amount.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $25,000 for East Bay Agency for Children to provide therapy at Rudsdale Newcomer High
output.summary: East Bay Agency for Children will offer therapy and case management to students at Rudsdale Newcomer High School who have Medi-Cal or are moving onto it. The agreement is up to $25,000 from August 3, 2020 to June 30, 2021. The Board is approving it after it began.

output.headline: Pays Bay Area Community Resources up to $60,000 for its Young Hawks newcomer student program
output.summary: Bay Area Community Resources will run the Young Hawks Program for newcomer students, with academic support, family engagement, a summer school program for English Learners, violence prevention, counseling and court advocacy. The agreement is up to $60,000 from August 31, 2020 to May 28, 2021, which began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $30,000 for a consultant to facilitate Strong Workforce career education projects
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The title says the agreement year is 2020-2020, but the action text says 2020-2021.
output.summary: A consultant will facilitate Strong Workforce and other Career Technical Education projects, funded by the K12 Strong Workforce Grant. The agreement is up to $30,000 from July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021. The Board is approving it after it began.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $35,000 for an arts consultant to help build the district's Strategic Arts Blueprint
output.summary: A consultant will work with the Visual and Performing Arts (VAPA) team to plan and carry out support structures that help district schools use the arts to improve learning. The agreement is up to $35,000 from August 3, 2020 to June 30, 2021. The Board is approving it after it began.

output.headline: Updates five administrative job descriptions and creates an Accounts Payable Technician III job
output.summary: The Board revises job descriptions for the Director of the Office of Ombudsperson, Deputy Director of the Office of Charter Schools, Director of Payroll, Director of Budget and Finance, and Coordinator of Pre-K Systems and Operations. It also creates a new job description for Accounts Payable Technician III. No dollar amount is listed.

output.headline: Ratifies $9,900 for Be a Mentor to host vendor background checks for up to 120 vendors
output.summary: The district pays Be a Mentor, Inc. up to $9,900 for software that tracks vendors and runs background clearances, with alerts if a vendor is later arrested. It covers up to 120 district vendors from July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021. The Board is approving this after the agreement's start date.

output.headline: Ratifies no-cost deal with Oakland Public Education Fund to survey families and give out devices
output.summary: Oakland Public Education Fund, through its Tech Exchange Project, will survey district families about their need for devices and help distribute computers and Wi-Fi hotspots to students. The two sides will also share data to track which students received devices. It costs the district nothing and runs from August 3, 2020 to June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Updates Board Policy 0420.4 on charter schools to match state law changes from July 1, 2020
output.summary: The Board amends its charter schools philosophy policy, BP 0420.4, so it matches changes in state law that took effect July 1, 2020. The item comes from the Charters Committee and lists no cost.

output.headline: Amends Measure G1 spending plan and grant for Community School for Creative Change Charter School
schools: Community School for Creative Change Charter School
output.summary: The Board adopts a resolution on a recommendation from the Measure G1 oversight commission. It amends the 2020-21 charter middle school grant application and education spending plan for Community School for Creative Change Charter School, using that year's approved funding. No dollar amount is listed.

output.headline: Extends Development Group's time to finish E-Rate technology work, with no added money
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The title mentions a matching funds appropriation and awarding a bid, but the action text only approves a contractor time extension for an existing E-Rate contract.
output.summary: This changes an existing contract with Development Group, Inc. for technology equipment and services under the district's 2019-20 federal E-Rate (school technology discount) application. It only gives the contractor more time because of COVID-19. All other terms stay the same and no money is added.
